title: Capacity Slicing Workshop and Contingency Staffing Playbook
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: Produce a repeatable playbook and run a cross-functional workshop to finalize scope and staffing allocations for Cycle 53. Output must include a prioritized scope slice (must/should/could), a contingency staffing plan (internal + contractors), and explicit SLOs that map to OKRs so PM/Eng/design can negotiate trade-offs.

Why: Recent cycles showed recurrent schedule creep when backend inference optimizations collide with console UX work. We need a defensible capacity model so releases align with committed SLAs and customer-impact priorities.

Scope:
- Run a 2-hour workshop with Eng leads (runtime, infra, console), Design, and Solutions to produce a candidate slice.
- Create a staffing matrix showing baseline FTE allocation, 20% buffer reserve, and named contractor roles for burst.
- Define automated rules for scope cuts if we hit velocity thresholds (e.g., 60% of planned story points by week 3 triggers mandatory cut of 'could' items).
- Produce an artifacts pack: Confluence playbook, a one-page roadmap for execs, and a dashboard tile for cycle burn vs. capacity.

Deliverables:
- Playbook doc (Confluence) with step-by-step workshop facilitation notes and decision rubric.
- Prioritized scope list (CSV) with OKR mapping and rollback policy.
- Staffing matrix (sheet) with FTE, contractors, estimates, and cost delta.
- Dashboard tile spec for Console (cost & velocity metrics) and a sample dashboard link.

Constraints & Assumptions:
- Hiring freezes for Q1; contractor budget available up to $40k for cycle.
- Eng estimate velocity based on last 3 cycles (avg 210 story points; we plan for 180 to be conservative).
- Customer-impact scoring uses existing rubric (0-5) from 2025-OKR playbook.

Success criteria:
- Workshop produces a committed scope with sign-off from Eng lead, Design lead, and PM director within 72 hours.
- No more than one P0 regression caused by scope overcommit in the cycle.
- Dashboard reflects real-time burn within 48 hours of beginning the cycle.
